title: State pattern
summary: Inputs mean different things in different states.

cards.title: The bug-prone way
cards.body: `if (jumpPressed && !isJumping && !isDucking) ...` Every new move adds flags, and the combinations explode. Bugs like double-jumps hide in those combinations.
Each node is a class. An input either changes the state or is ignored, decided by the current state alone.
The Slot Lab machine used an `enum` and `if`s: perfect for 5 states. Classes pay off when each state has its own data and per-frame logic.

cards.question: The hero is Ducking and JUMP is pressed. With this design, what happens?
cards.explain: Ducking::handle only reacts to releasing DOWN. Any other input returns nullptr: stay in the same state.
